title: Two Sforza cipher letters of 4 May 1446: reply to Zorzo del Maino (BnF italien 1583 f. 68; DECODE R7898) and Amidani to Sforza (f. 70; R7899 P1)

steps.what: Downloaded the DECODE R7898 image with the saved cookie; dated in clear M cccc xlvj die iiij may (4 May 1446), mixed clear Lombard Italian and graphic cipher.

Mazzatinti's inventory of BnF ital. 1583-1593 (Archivio storico lombardo X, 1883): f. 68 = reply to what Zorzo Maino reported, in cipher; f. 70 = Vincenzo Amidani to Sforza, Milan 4 May, in cipher. No reading printed.
Draft transcription of f. 68: 404 signs, 26 types after merging diacritic variants.

Homophonic annealing with it-cinquecento, clear text as context: unconstrained, capped homophones, nulls allowed, then one-to-one swaps (solver verified on a 400-letter synthetic cipher). All nonsense or degenerate.
Word-pattern search on repeats (FpBHcdSp x2, 8zBprJFp x2, xJpg x4): FpBHcdSp fits 'uisconti' but the other repeats contradict that key.
Found f. 70 (Amidani, same day, same sign family) on DECODE R7899 image P1; transcribed 390 signs; annealing on it alone also gives nonsense.

Downloaded all 208 Sforza key records on DECODE (ASMi Carteggio Sforzesco cart. 1591, 1597, 1598) and scanned them at thumbnail size; read the headings and alphabets of the 15th-c. copies (cart. 1597 nos. 2-36). 1597 no. 14 (18th-c. copy, 'Angelus cum cifra Vincentij', shared with Stavoli, Augustinus, Baptista, Matheus, Vincentius) is the same family: homophones, vowel+consonant syllable signs, word signs (de = cross-circle, ot = divide sign), nulls. Its letter signs do not match the frequent signs of f. 68 or f. 70. 1597 no. 17 (1447, Sforza's envoys to Alfonso) does not match either.
George Lasry transcribed f. 68 (DECODE R7898) and f. 70 (R7899 image P1) with CTTS: 827 cipher boxes, 12 clear boxes, 65 sign classes (PR #60).
CTTS generated the initial key from the ciphertext of both letters (George Lasry); no outside key or plaintext.

Astra and Fable 5.1 refined the key and the reading (PR #60): CHE, CON, ET, PER, QVA, SE word signs; provisional (8)=l, (24)=n, (16)=in; edition and English translation of both letters; 780 of 827 occurrences assigned, 47 unresolved.

lasry2026/verify.py re-run: both CTTS exports, all 839 boxes, the edited segments and all checksums pass. First cipher line agrees with Mazzatinti's 1883 heading (reply to Zorzo Maino); f. 70 date line deciphers as 'mediolani die qvarto mai', matching Mazzatinti's Milan, 4 May.
Measured sense (measure_sense.py): f. 68 380/425, f. 70 341/402, both 721/827 = 87.2% of cipher tokens read as sense (assignment 94.3%); below the 95% read bar.

Escalation (extend_open.py): every letter, word value and null tried for the 14 open classes and 3 provisional ones, both letters scored with it-cinquecento. No letter value wins by a usable margin; nothing adopted.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 780 tokens, 51 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -2.07 per letter; random keys -3.761 (z 5.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.544 (mean -2.567, z 26.2); annealer on the real text -2.415. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): it1583: George Lasry's CTTS files from PR #60 linked: ctts/transcription and ctts/decryption per letter, his edited readings (edited.txt, companion/edited.txt), full_letter.md (edition with English translation) and ctts/key.txt.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): edited.txt, companion/edited.txt and full_letter.md read. f. 68 builds sentences with holes at line openings (C overturned to B); f. 70 has holes in every clause of lines 1-5 (C confirmed), relabelled decoded, not read. Class read in part kept; fraction_read 0.9432 -> 0.514.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b29): DECODE R7899 fetched (P1 the f. 70 slip; P2 an address leaf to Francesco Sforza, not f. 70's); every sign of f. 70 re-checked on P1 against Lasry's CTTS overlay: labels confirmed, none changed. The clear words of lines 2 and 6 stay uncertain on the binarized photograph.

The sixteen sibling 1446 records of ital. 1583 (R7900-R7915) fetched and viewed: none uses the f. 68/f. 70 sign alphabet. Found: R7900 (f. 89, Angelus, 30 Sept 1446, headed 'Cum cifra Vincentii') and R7901 (f. 90) are the same despatch in cipher and in clear, a contemporary decipherment of the Vincentius cipher (the ASMi cart. 1597 no. 14 key), a different alphabet from f. 70.

#30 adopted as a null: 8 occurrences across f. 68 and f. 70, all at word or phrase boundaries, no letter value makes a word at any. #25 as null (9 of 10 at boundaries) and the sense values (25)=Duca, (19)=ordine, (26)=gente flagged for review, not adopted. Partial reading texts/f70_partial_reading.md: 0.50 clean sentences (5/10), explicit holes 0.70; the news clause of lines 4-5 does not build and the signature is unread: stays decoded, not read.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.07; polyphony 0.0; 47 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.415

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry generated the initial key with CTTS from the ciphertext of both letters and Astra and Fable 5.1 refined it; no outside key fits (208 Sforza keys checked in Sept 2026) and no decipherment or plaintext of the cipher exists.
outcome.notes: Both letters read in part with one key: 87.2% of cipher tokens read as sense. Earlier 'closed unread' (21 Sept 2026) superseded by the contributed CTTS key. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: f. 68 reads (C overturned to B); f. 70 decoded, not read; fraction_read 0.9432 (assigned) -> 0.514 (tokens in the letter that reads).

outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit, 22 Oct 2026: f. 68 (R7898, 425 cipher tokens, lasry2026/cipher_tokens.txt) reads; f. 70 (402 tokens) is decoded, not read: 425 of 827 = 0.514. The earlier 0.9432 (edition.json via measure_sense.py: 780 of 827 tokens assigned) is withdrawn as a reading figure.

gaps.item: 39 unresolved occurrences in 13 sign classes (#30, 8 occurrences, adopted as a null 23 Oct 2026), mostly at line and paragraph openings
gaps.detail: Probably nulls, titles or abbreviations; LM pass could not fix them; the sixteen sibling 1446 records R7900-R7915 were opened 23 Oct (b29) and none uses this alphabet; no key among the 208 Sforza key records.
Assigned letters do not form a name; Amidani attribution from Mazzatinti only; same open classes.

gaps.detail: Each rests on one or two occurrences; no further occurrences in any sibling.
Binarized scan of f. 68 and a DECODE photograph of f. 70 only.

Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b29, texts/f70_reread_log.md): labels confirmed on R7899 P1; the news clause of lines 4-5 rests on (25), (19), (26), #25, (4), which have no key value; sense hypotheses flagged, not adopted.

texts.label: f. 68 (DECODE R7898), 4 May 1446, reply concerning Zorzo del Maino's report
texts.summary: An unidentified writer replies to Zorzo del Maino's report concerning Count Francesco (probably Francesco Sforza): the count's obligations to others are his own affair, the writer seeks only God's honour and his own security, and asks for eight or ten names in writing from which trusted intermediaries could be chosen.

reading_review.note: Overturns the per-document C. The edited text and Lasry's English translation build sentences from line 2 to line 11 (Zorzo del Maino's report, the count's obligations, "la secvreza nostra", eight or ten names); the ? runs sit at line openings and ends, where NOTES and the gap list take them for nulls or titles, and two mid-sentence holes (l. 10 "?intita", l. 11) are scattered.

texts.label: f. 70 (DECODE R7899 image P1), Milan, 4 May 1446, catalogued as Vincenzo Amidani to Francesco Sforza
texts.summary: The writer reports prospective action against Cremona and how the Venetian government might declare itself, with help, defence and troops soon in the field, and closes that he writes to do his duty; dated Milan, the fourth of May; the signature is unread.
texts.note: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b29), still not read: every sign of lines 1-8 checked on DECODE image P1 against Lasry's overlay (labels confirmed, none changed); #30 adopted as a null (8 boundary occurrences in both letters); partial reading texts/f70_partial_reading.md scores 0.50 clean sentences (explicit holes 0.70), but the news clause of lines 4-5 ('che se e reunito [#25] [(4)] [(25)] da [(19)] ad tute le sue [(26)]') does not build and the signature is unread. Blocker: no-key-material: the open classes (25), (19), (26), #25, (4), (6), (22) have no key value, no decipherment exists, and none of the sixteen sibling 1446 records R7900-R7915 nor the 208 Sforza key records uses this alphabet. Sense hypotheses (25)=Duca, (19)=ordine, (26)=gente are flagged for review, not adopted.

prior.where: Mazzatinti's 1883 inventory lists both as 'in cifre' with headings only; no edition or decipherment found
